clue.text: One approaching fifty left a tropical sort of fruit

indicators.note: a sort of version of these letters is a rearranged one, so the remaining letters are shuffled
left in the sense of departed, so these letters go away from the words before them
one piece comes right up to the next, so the letter for one sits just before the letter for fifty

parts.note: one can be the indefinite article a
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Someone nearing fifty has gone off to some tropical place, oddly linked to fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' removes AL ('One' A 'approaching' fifty, L) from the end of A TROPICAL, leaving ATROPIC, and 'sort of' rearranges those seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An apricot is a soft orange stone fruit, a close relative of the peach.

clue.text: Flabbergasted but not all at the same time

definitions.text: not all at the same time

explanation.surface: Someone astonished, but not every person at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Flabbergasted people are amazed and reeling; staggered shifts or breaks are spread out so they begin at different times.

clue.text: Maintain disruptive sit-ins

indicators.note: something disruptive throws things into disorder, so the letters of the protest word are jumbled

explanation.surface: Protesters claim their sit-ins are meant to cause disruption.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain a claim is to assert it firmly and keep repeating it.

clue.text: Now and then completely recovered

parts.note: someone recovered from illness is fit again
completely means fully

explanation.surface: A patient who seems sometimes fully recovered and sometimes not.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue says 'completely recovered', fully fit, but the two words go in the grid the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something fitfully means doing it in irregular bursts, only occasionally.

clue.text: Relatively congenial meeting?

parts.note: relatively is read as to do with relatives, and congenial as people of one kin, so this is an occasion when kin get together

explanation.surface: A get-together that is moderately pleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: A reunion of relations such as a wedding party or Christmas lunch is a meeting of kin.

clue.text: Money said to be common on the island

indicators.note: said signals that the words are heard spoken rather than read on the page

parts.note: a tenner is a ten-pound note, British slang for money
something rife is common and widespread

explanation.surface: Cash is said to be plentiful on a certain island.
explanation.walkthrough: A tenner is a British ten-pound note; 'said to be' makes it a sound, TENE, and RIFE follows as written, giving the largest of the Canary Islands.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenerife is a Spanish island in the Canaries, off north-west Africa.

clue.text: Dark, not starting to be illuminated by a star during daytime

indicators.note: not starting means the word loses its opening letter

parts.words: illuminated by a star during daytime
parts.note: lit up by our star, the sun, in daylight

explanation.surface: A dark sky with no star shining by day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not starting' drops the S from SUNLIT; the star in question is the Sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Unlit means without any light, hence in darkness.

clue.text: The Parisian repeatedly going round south Carolina to a famous opera-house!

indicators.note: one piece goes round the other, so the doubled article encloses the rest
repeatedly means the French word is used twice

parts.note: la is the French feminine form of the
SC is the postal abbreviation for South Carolina

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman keeps travelling round the American South on the way to a celebrated opera house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeatedly' doubles the French feminine article, and 'going round' wraps the pair about the state abbreviation plus the clue's own A.
explanation.definitionFit: La Scala in Milan is one of the world's best-known theatres for opera.

clue.text: Place with no return on target

parts.note: a spot is a place

indicators.note: return here means the little word comes back, read from right to left

explanation.surface: Somewhere with no comeback is right on target.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' reads the little word backwards; 'with' is only a link joining the two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Spot on is a British idiom for exactly right or precisely accurate.

clue.text: Don't worry unnecessarily, stupid

explanation.surface: Advice to stop fretting, delivered with a parting insult.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as two words, the first sense is an instruction to bother oneself less.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it tells you to be bothered less; as one word it means thoughtless or foolish.

clue.text: After having fish I take one masculine Parisian round one for pasta

parts.note: ling is a long-bodied sea fish

indicators.note: round means one piece encloses the other

parts.note: un is the French masculine word for one
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: After a fish course, a diner takes a Frenchman out for some pasta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts I inside UN to give UIN; the final I is the clue's own I.
explanation.definitionFit: Linguine are long flat ribbons of pasta, a little narrower than tagliatelle.

clue.text: Scoundrel had brown cane

parts.note: a rat is a scoundrel or traitor
tan is a light brown colour

explanation.surface: The villain carried a brown walking stick.
explanation.definitionFit: Rattan is the stem of a climbing palm, used as cane for furniture and walking sticks.

clue.text: After words of warning, attempt to do some work in the wood

indicators.note: after puts the attempt following the warnings in the word

parts.note: golfers shout fore as a warning, so several such shouts are fores
to try is to attempt to do something

explanation.surface: After a shout of warning, someone tries a bit of woodland work.
explanation.walkthrough: FORE is the golfer's shout warning that a ball is coming.
explanation.definitionFit: Forestry is the management of woodland: planting, tending and felling trees.

clue.text: Put into some coloured paper presently?

definitions.text: Put into some coloured paper presently?

parts.words: Put into some coloured paper presently?
parts.note: presently is read as in the manner of a present, so the act is wrapping a present in bright paper

explanation.surface: An instruction to put something into coloured paper soon.
explanation.definitionFit: Gifts are wrapped in decorative paper before being given.

clue.text: Resist having support

parts.note: with means having, as in a man with a hat
a stand is a support

explanation.surface: Fighting back with a little backing.
explanation.definitionFit: To withstand something is to hold out against it, to resist it.

clue.text: Essential that movement is slow in this part of Florida

parts.note: key means essential or crucial
largo is a musical direction meaning slow, used for a slow movement

explanation.surface: Life moves slowly in a certain corner of Florida.
explanation.walkthrough: Key Largo is an island in the Florida Keys.
explanation.definitionFit: Key Largo is the longest island of the Florida Keys, south of Miami.

clue.text: Dictates metamorphosis in the final analysis

indicators.note: a metamorphosis is a total change of form, so the letters are transformed into a new order

explanation.surface: Orders are rewritten once everything is finally weighed up.
explanation.definitionFit: An acid test is a decisive trial that settles the matter, from the old way of testing gold with acid.

clue.text: Organised romance in Italy

indicators.note: organised means arranged afresh, so the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A love affair is being arranged somewhere in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Cremona is a city in Lombardy, northern Italy, famous for violin makers.

clue.text: Intoxicant cool Hal fermented

indicators.note: fermented means worked up or agitated, so the letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Cool Hal brewed something strong.
explanation.definitionFit: Alcohol is the substance in drinks that makes people drunk.

clue.text: Dance hoops

explanation.surface: A dance with hoops.
explanation.walkthrough: Hula hoops are the plastic hoops twirled round the waist; the doubled name serves for both the dance and the hoop.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hawaiian swaying dance is the hula; the toy rings spun round the hips share the hula name.

clue.text: Look at two articles with hate

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
a is the indefinite article
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Glaring at two items with loathing.
explanation.walkthrough: LO is the old exclamation meaning look; the two articles are the indefinite and the definite.
explanation.definitionFit: To loathe something is to detest it intensely.

clue.text: Daughter twisted ankle outside in Cumbria

indicators.note: outside means the reshaped word wraps round the single letter
an ankle that is twisted is turned awry, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A girl turns her ankle while out walking in the Lake District.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisted' turns ANKLE into KENAL and 'outside' puts it round D. Cumbria is a county in north-west England, home of the Lake District.
explanation.definitionFit: Kendal is a market town in Cumbria, known for its mint cake.

clue.text: Dutch jazz fan produced old coin

parts.note: cat is old slang for a jazz enthusiast

explanation.surface: A Dutch jazz lover pulls out an antique coin.
explanation.definitionFit: The ducat was a gold or silver coin used across Europe in earlier centuries.

clue.text: Response concerning battle

parts.note: re means concerning, as in business letters
action is fighting, a battle

explanation.surface: A reply about a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A reaction is a reply or answer to something that has happened.

clue.text: Not north American musical instrument used in orchestral compositions

indicators.note: not means the letters that follow are left out of the instrument

parts.note: a concertina is a small hexagonal squeezebox

explanation.surface: No North American instrument is used in these orchestral works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not' removes N and A from the end of CONCERTINA.
explanation.definitionFit: Concertos are works for solo instrument and orchestra; this is the Italian plural.

clue.text: German man has order for cab

parts.note: Hans is a common German man's name
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A German fellow orders a taxi.
explanation.walkthrough: The OM, Order of Merit, is a British honour limited to a few members.
explanation.definitionFit: A hansom is a two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage for hire, the Victorian taxi.

clue.text: Fuss after some of the madrigal

indicators.note: after places the fuss behind the portion in the word

parts.note: a part is some of something
song, as in song and dance, means a fuss

explanation.surface: A row breaks out after a piece of the madrigal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Song and dance' is an idiom for a fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: A madrigal is an unaccompanied piece for several voices, a type of part song.
